title: Touch Control Failure
shortDescription: The touch control board has detected a button stuck or a short.
fullDescription:
F1 on an LG cooktop indicates the touch control board has detected a stuck key or a short circuit in the touch matrix. The cooktop locks out to prevent unintended operation.

Common causes include water or spills on the glass, a cracked touch sensor, or a failing control PCB. A thorough cleaning and power cycle often resolves transient cases, but persistent F1 requires board inspection.

The touch board is mounted directly under the glass at the front edge of the cooktop.

causes.cause: Moisture or spills on control surface

fixSteps.title: Clean the surface
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe glass completely dry with a lint-free cloth.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off the breaker for 5 minutes and restore power.

fixSteps.title: Inspect glass
fixSteps.instruction: Look for cracks near touch icons that could affect the sensor.

fixSteps.title: Replace touch board
fixSteps.instruction: If code persists, replace the touch control PCB under the glass.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if the glass is cracked or you are uncomfortable removing the cooktop from the countertop.

faq.q: Can I still use the cooktop with F1?
faq.a: No, controls are locked for safety.
Yes, even small amounts near the touch sensors trigger F1.

title: Overheating Detected
shortDescription: The cooktop has detected excessive temperature on one of the burners or the control board.
fullDescription:
F2 indicates the cooktop has sensed an over-temperature condition, typically in the element or near the control PCB. Induction cooktops have multiple sensors to protect components; F2 is triggered when any of them exceeds safety thresholds.

Common causes include blocked cooling vents, a failing cooling fan, or ambient heat exceeding spec. On electric radiant cooktops it may also indicate a bad element temperature limiter.

Allow the cooktop to fully cool, clear any obstructions, then power cycle before further diagnosis.

fixSteps.title: Let cooktop cool
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off and allow 30 minutes of cool-down time.

fixSteps.title: Clear obstructions
fixSteps.instruction: Check under-cabinet vents and clear debris.

fixSteps.title: Verify installation
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure cooktop has required clearance per LG manual.

fixSteps.title: Test cooling fan
fixSteps.instruction: If fan is silent or weak, replace the cooling fan assembly.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if F2 returns after cleaning vents and confirming fan operation.

faq.q: Is the cooktop dangerous with F2?
faq.a: No, the protection circuit has already shut down heating.
Typically 1 inch below and proper cabinet cutout; see your install manual.

title: Element Temperature Sensor Fault
shortDescription: A burner temperature sensor is open or short-circuited.
fullDescription:
F3 points to a fault on the temperature sensor of one of the cooking zones. The sensor normally reports element temperature to the control board; an open or short circuit causes F3 and disables that burner.

On induction cooktops, this is the NTC thermistor pressed against the underside of the ceramic glass. On radiant cooktops, it may be the limit thermostat wired to the heating element.

Replacement usually requires lifting the cooktop out of the countertop and accessing the module from below.

fixSteps.title: Shut off breaker
fixSteps.instruction: Cut power at the breaker before service.

fixSteps.title: Access underside
fixSteps.instruction: Remove cooktop from countertop and access the affected burner module.

fixSteps.title: Test sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Measure NTC resistance; open or shorted readings indicate failure.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install replacement sensor, reseat harness, and reinstall cooktop.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if you cannot safely remove the cooktop from the countertop.

faq.a: Usually yes, only the affected zone is disabled.

faq.q: Can I replace the sensor from above?
faq.a: No, access is from below the cooktop.

title: Power Module Fault
shortDescription: An inverter or relay power module has reported a fault.
fullDescription:
F4 indicates a failure in one of the power modules that switches the heating element or induction coil. The main board has detected an unexpected output state — typically a relay welded closed, a failed IGBT, or an over-current event.

This fault disables the affected burner and, in severe cases, the entire cooktop. Because the power module handles high current, diagnosis requires caution and electrical expertise.

Replacement power modules are model-specific and often sold as a complete board assembly.

fixSteps.title: Shut off power
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off cooktop breaker immediately.

fixSteps.title: Inspect for damage
fixSteps.instruction: Remove cooktop and inspect power module for burn marks.

fixSteps.title: Test element
fixSteps.instruction: Verify element is not shorted before replacing board.

fixSteps.title: Replace module
fixSteps.instruction: Install replacement power board — best left to a trained technician.

whenToCallPro: Always call a pro — power module work involves high voltage and can be dangerous.

faq.q: Is it safe to keep using the cooktop?
faq.a: No, shut off the breaker until repaired.
Only under repeated over-current or lightning damage scenarios.

title: Voltage Out of Range
shortDescription: The cooktop detects supply voltage outside its operating window.
fullDescription:
F5 indicates the main board sees line voltage outside the nominal 208-240V range required for safe operation. Too-low voltage can stress components, while too-high voltage risks damage.

Typical causes are loose connections at the junction box, utility voltage issues, or a failing main board that misreads the line. If other appliances on the same circuit work fine, suspect the cooktop's wiring or board.

Verification requires a multimeter check at the cooktop terminal block with the appliance off.

causes.cause: Loose line connection at terminal block
Failed voltage sensing on main board

fixSteps.title: Check breaker
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect and reset cooktop breaker if needed.

fixSteps.title: Measure at outlet
fixSteps.instruction: With cooktop disconnected, measure voltage at the junction box — expect 240V ±5%.

fixSteps.title: Tighten terminals
fixSteps.instruction: Shut off power, remove terminal block cover, and torque connections to spec.

fixSteps.title: Call utility
fixSteps.instruction: If supply voltage is out of range, contact your power company.

whenToCallPro: Call an electrician if connections are tight and voltage is still out of range.

faq.q: Can I reset F5 by power cycling?
faq.a: Only temporarily if the voltage has since recovered.

faq.q: Does F5 mean my wiring is bad?
faq.a: Often yes; tighten connections and measure voltage before assuming a board fault.

title: Cooling Fan Fault
shortDescription: The internal cooling fan is not running at expected speed.
fullDescription:
F6 appears when the main board cannot confirm the cooling fan is spinning. Induction and high-power radiant cooktops rely on this fan to prevent electronics overheating.

Causes include debris in the fan, a failing motor, or a disconnected harness. If left to run, the cooktop will soon escalate to F2 over-temperature and shut down entirely.

Service requires pulling the cooktop out and accessing the fan on the underside.

fixSteps.title: Power off
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off cooktop breaker.

fixSteps.title: Access fan
fixSteps.instruction: Lift cooktop and locate the cooling fan on the chassis.

fixSteps.title: Clean and test
fixSteps.instruction: Vacuum debris and spin blade to check for binding.

fixSteps.title: Replace motor
fixSteps.instruction: If fan fails to spin, install a replacement.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if you're not comfortable lifting the cooktop or working under the countertop.

faq.q: How often does the fan fail?
faq.a: It's among the more common induction cooktop failures after 5+ years.
No, modern fans are sealed; replace if they squeak or stall.

title: Communication Error
shortDescription: Loss of communication between cooktop boards.
fullDescription:
F7 indicates the main control board has lost communication with the user interface or a secondary power module. Most LG cooktops use multiple communicating boards, and a break in the link triggers F7.

Causes include loose ribbon cables, damaged connectors after spills reaching underneath, or a failed board. Intermittent F7 is often a connector issue, while persistent F7 points to a board.

Diagnosis requires lifting the cooktop, reseating every connector, and re-testing.

fixSteps.title: Power off
fixSteps.instruction: Shut off breaker.

fixSteps.title: Lift cooktop
fixSteps.instruction: Carefully raise the cooktop and expose the control area.

fixSteps.title: Reseat connectors
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect and reseat every ribbon and harness connector.

fixSteps.title: Replace affected board
fixSteps.instruction: If F7 persists, replace the UI board first, then main board.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro for board-level diagnostics or if reseating connectors doesn't clear the code.

faq.q: Is F7 always a board replacement?
faq.a: Not always; cable reseating resolves many cases.
Yes, liquid seeping under the glass can reach connectors.

title: Pan Detection Error
shortDescription: Induction cooktop cannot detect a compatible pan.
fullDescription:
F8 on an LG induction cooktop means the zone cannot detect a ferromagnetic pan. Induction cooking requires cookware that a magnet will stick to; copper, aluminum, and most glass cookware won't work.

Other causes include a pan smaller than the minimum zone diameter, a pan with a warped or non-flat bottom, or a failing pan detection circuit.

Try a different pan before assuming a hardware fault.

fixSteps.title: Test cookware
fixSteps.instruction: Stick a magnet to the pan bottom; if it doesn't hold firmly, it's not induction-compatible.

fixSteps.title: Check size
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure pan diameter meets the zone minimum (usually 4.7 in / 12 cm).

fixSteps.title: Try different pan
fixSteps.instruction: Test with a known good induction pan.

fixSteps.title: Service call
fixSteps.instruction: If issue persists with known good cookware, call LG service.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro only if F8 occurs with confirmed induction-compatible cookware.
videoSearchQuery: LG cooktop F8 pan detection fix

faq.a: Cast iron and magnetic stainless steel. A magnet should stick firmly to the bottom.

faq.q: Why does my old pan suddenly not work?
faq.a: Warped bottoms lose contact; try a flat pan.

title: Ground Fault Detected
shortDescription: The cooktop has detected a ground fault in the element or wiring.
fullDescription:
F9 indicates the cooktop's ground fault detection circuit has triggered. Current is leaking to ground, often through a degraded heating element, pinched wire, or moisture intrusion.

This is a safety fault — the cooktop disables the affected zone (or all zones) to prevent shock hazard. F9 should not be ignored or bypassed.

Diagnosis requires megohm testing of element windings and visual inspection of wiring.

fixSteps.title: Cut power
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off breaker immediately.

fixSteps.title: Dry and inspect
fixSteps.instruction: Let cooktop fully dry 24 hours if moisture is suspected.

fixSteps.title: Test elements
fixSteps.instruction: Megohm-test each heating element to ground — infinite resistance is correct.

fixSteps.title: Replace faulty part
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the element or wiring found to be leaking.

whenToCallPro: Always call a pro — ground faults are a shock hazard and require proper testing equipment.
videoSearchQuery: LG cooktop F9 ground fault fix

faq.a: Yes — shut off the breaker and do not use until repaired.
If it reaches terminals, yes. Let fully dry before retesting.

title: Generic Error
shortDescription: General error; check display for additional characters.
fullDescription:
Er on an LG cooktop is a generic error banner usually followed by a specific code (e.g., Er F1). If only Er appears, the control board has failed to parse the specific fault or a sensor link is down.

Start with a power cycle and check that the display shows the full code after restart. If only Er appears consistently, the main board likely needs service.

Capture a photo of the display when the error appears to aid diagnosis.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Shut off breaker 5 minutes, then restore.

fixSteps.title: Observe
fixSteps.instruction: Note whether Er is followed by another code.

fixSteps.title: Clean controls
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure no moisture or debris is on the touch area.

fixSteps.title: Call service
fixSteps.instruction: If Er persists, request LG service for diagnosis.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if power cycling does not reveal a specific code.

faq.q: Does Er mean my cooktop is broken?
faq.a: Not necessarily; a power cycle often clears transient errors.
Yes, a short video helps a technician diagnose remotely.

title: Child Lock Active
shortDescription: The child lock feature is engaged and must be released before use.
fullDescription:
LC on the LG cooktop display indicates Lock/Child Lock mode is active. The controls are intentionally disabled to prevent unintended operation by children or pets walking on the surface.

This is not a fault — it's a feature. To clear, press and hold the Lock button (usually for 3 seconds) until LC disappears and a confirmation tone sounds.

Some models use a different button combo; consult the quick-reference guide printed near the controls.

fixSteps.title: Press and hold Lock
fixSteps.instruction: Press and hold the Lock button for 3-5 seconds.

fixSteps.title: Confirm release
fixSteps.instruction: Listen for tone and watch for LC to clear.

fixSteps.title: Clean controls
fixSteps.instruction: If LC won't clear, clean the surface — spills can register as button presses.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: If stuck, shut off breaker for 5 minutes and retry.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro only if the Lock button physically fails to respond.
videoSearchQuery: LG cooktop LC child lock off

faq.a: No, it's a user feature indicating child lock is active.

faq.q: How do I disable it permanently?
faq.a: You can't — LC must be released each time it's activated, but you can avoid activating it.

title: Cooling Mode Indicator
shortDescription: The cooktop internal components are in a forced cool-down state.
fullDescription:
The C indicator (sometimes shown as flashing C) means the cooktop's internal electronics are in a cool-down cycle, typically after prolonged high-power use. The cooling fan will run even though no burner is active.

This is normal protective behavior and clears automatically when internal temperature drops below threshold, usually within 5-15 minutes.

If C persists for more than 30 minutes with no cooking activity, suspect a cooling fan or temperature sensor fault.
symptoms: Fan running with no burner on

fixSteps.title: Wait it out
fixSteps.instruction: Allow 5-15 minutes for cool-down to complete.

fixSteps.title: Check vents
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure cabinet vents aren't blocked.

fixSteps.title: Test fan
fixSteps.instruction: If C lasts longer than 30 min, inspect cooling fan operation.

fixSteps.title: Service call
fixSteps.instruction: Contact LG if fan runs but C won't clear.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if C persists beyond 30 minutes or recurs without cooking.

faq.a: Usually not — it just means the cooktop is cooling itself.

faq.q: Can I use the cooktop while C shows?
faq.a: Some zones may remain disabled until cool-down finishes.
